eyebrow: cache() — don't recompute the same thing twice
code:
cleaned = trips.filter(col("fare_amount") > 0).na.drop(subset=["passenger_count"])
cleaned.cache()

print(cleaned.count())
print(cleaned.filter(col("trip_distance") > 10).count())  # reuses the cache
caption: Every action normally re-runs the whole lazy plan (Lesson 34) -- cache() stops that.

code:
trips.repartition(20)   # can increase OR decrease; always shuffles
trips.coalesce(4)       # can only decrease; avoids a full shuffle
caption: coalesce() is the cheaper choice for reducing partition count before a final write.

code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast

result = trips.join(
  broadcast(zones), trips.PULocationID == zones.LocationID, "left"
)
caption: Sends the small side to every worker, instead of shuffling the giant side.
